inline_comments.comment:
`fs.watch` with `{ recursive: true }` is not supported on Linux. On Linux, Node.js either silently ignores the flag (older versions) or throws `EINVAL`/`ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM` (Node 22+). The `catch` block only logs at debug level and continues — so on Linux, **no directory is ever watched**, and the dev server will not pick up any file changes without a restart.

Consider using a cross-platform watcher library (e.g. `chokidar`, which Storybook already uses elsewhere) or fall back to non-recursive watching by walking the directory tree manually on Linux (`process.platform !== 'darwin' && process.platform !== 'win32'`).

The static `instance` Promise is never cleared. If `dispose()` is called (e.g. in tests or on server shutdown) and then `getInstance()` is called again, it returns the already-disposed manager instead of creating a fresh one. The disposed manager has cleared its `configProjects`, `fsFileSnapshots`, etc., so any subsequent extraction will silently return empty results.

Fix: set `ComponentMetaManager.instance = undefined` inside `dispose()`, or (safer) have `dispose()` only clear internal state and let the singleton remain valid.

`getCommandLine()` is called immediately (to get the initial `commandLine` for the constructor) and then the same closure is passed as `getCommandLineFn`. This causes `parseConfigWorker` — which reads and parses the tsconfig — to run **twice** on every project creation. Store the result of the first call and reuse it:
```ts
const initialCommandLine = this.parseConfigWorker(tsconfig);
project = new ComponentMetaProject(
  this.typescript,
  initialCommandLine,
  tsconfig,
  this.fsFileSnapshots,
  () => this.parseConfigWorker(tsconfig)
);
```

When multiple entries share the same `componentPath`, `serializeComponentDocs` is called once using `first.componentSourceFile` and `first.defaultsSourcePath`. If different entries for the same component file were resolved via different story files (e.g. two stories import the same component, one resolving to the `.d.ts` declaration and the other to the `.tsx` source), only the first entry's metadata is used for defaults extraction. The less-common entry's `defaultsSourcePath` is silently discarded. Consider asserting or logging when `componentSourceFile` differs across entries in the same group.

The old `findMatchingComponent` checked `[it.componentName, it.localImportName, it.importName].includes(componentName)`. The new version only checks `it.componentName === componentName`. This can miss compound-component cases where `csf._meta.component` resolves to the base name (e.g. `"Accordion"`) but the CSF parser or `getComponents` stores the compound form as `componentName = "Accordion.Root"`. If the match fails, the component falls through to the title-based heuristic instead of returning an exact match. Verify with a story that has `meta.component = Namespace.Member` to confirm no regression.

`watch: boolean` in the `manifests` PresetPropertyFn type signature is non-optional, but `getManifests` can pass `watch: undefined` (the default parameter `{ watch?: boolean } = {}`). TypeScript will flag this when the two types are checked together. Change the type to `watch?: boolean` to match actual usage.

`execSync('cp -rL ...')`, `execSync('mkdir -p ...')`, and the `cleanup` function's `execSync('rm -rf ...')` are Unix-only commands and will fail on Windows CI. Consider replacing with Node's built-in cross-platform APIs:
- `fs.mkdirSync(dest, { recursive: true })` instead of `mkdir -p`
- `fs.cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true })` (Node 16.7+) instead of `cp -rL`
- `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` instead of `rm -rf`

In the `asyncCache` error handler, `store` is captured by closure. After `invalidateCache()` replaces `asyncMemoStore` with a new WeakMap, the captured `store` still references the old, now-orphaned Map. `store.delete(k)` successfully deletes from that orphaned Map — harmless, but it means the semantics of "drop rejected promise so retries can recompute" only works correctly for the current cache generation. Retries after an `invalidateCache()` call will always recompute regardless (new store, no entry), so the behaviour is correct by coincidence. A brief comment noting this subtlety would prevent future confusion.

general_comments.comment: The `extractDestructuringDefaults` / `serializeComponentDocs` path for compound-component members (when `memberAccess` is set) extracts defaults from the *namespace object's* declaration (e.g. `Accordion`), not from the member's declaration (`Accordion.Root`). For a namespace object like `export const Accordion = { Root, Item }`, no destructuring defaults exist on the namespace itself — they live inside `Root`'s function body. This means `defaultValue` will always be `null` for compound-component members even when the underlying component has destructuring defaults. This limitation is not documented in the JSDoc or PR description and may surprise consumers of the manifest.

The `manifests` function in `generator.ts` has grown substantially — it now orchestrates three docgen engines, async resolution, batching, and watching across ~180 lines. The three engine branches inside the per-entry mapping closure (`if docgenEngine === 'react-docgen' ... else if ... else`) are hard to follow and easy to diverge. Consider extracting a small `extractDocgenProps(engine, component, rcmResults, absoluteImportPath)` helper that returns `{ reactDocgen, reactDocgenTypescript, reactComponentMeta, docgenDescription, docgenError }`, keeping the main loop focused on manifest assembly.

The `ComponentMetaManager.batchExtract` stores results keyed by `storyFilePath` (which is set to `absoluteImportPath` — the story file). In `generator.ts` Step 3, the lookup is `rcmResults?.get(absoluteImportPath)`, which is correct. However, the field name `storyFilePath` in `StoryExtractionEntry` and the variable `absoluteImportPath` in `generator.ts` refer to the same value through two different names, creating a subtle coupling. If the key is ever changed to use the component path instead, the lookup in `generator.ts` would silently return `undefined` for all entries. A short comment at the `batchExtract` call site clarifying that `absoluteImportPath` is the story file (not the component file) would prevent future mismatches.
